title: Chapter 9 Drill: Gynecologic Oncology, Breast Disease, and Cancer Screening

items.stem: A 52-year-old woman underwent total hysterectomy with cervical removal for fibroids. Pathology was benign, and she has no history of CIN 2 or higher. What cervical screening is recommended?
items.explanation: After hysterectomy with removal of the cervix for a benign indication and no history of CIN 2 or higher, screening is not needed. Continued surveillance for at least 25 years applies to women whose hysterectomy was for high-grade precancer. Cytology or HPV testing would sample a tissue that no longer exists and produce false reassurance or false alarms.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 20 weeks of gestation is diagnosed with breast cancer and needs systemic therapy. The oncology team plans a regimen including trastuzumab. Which obstetric concern should guide counseling?
options: Neural tube defect from first-trimester exposure
Fetal bone marrow suppression at term only
items.explanation: Trastuzumab is avoided in pregnancy because it causes oligohydramnios and can harm the fetus. Tamoxifen is also avoided. Many cytotoxic regimens are acceptable in the second and third trimesters, stopped about 3 weeks before delivery. A neural tube defect arises with first-trimester exposure, not at 20 weeks, and the effect described is not limited to the mother.

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman who is Rh(D) negative has a complete hydatidiform mole evacuated at 14 weeks of gestation. What is the appropriate postprocedure treatment?
items.explanation: Trophoblastic tissue can express the D antigen, so Rh-negative women receive Rh immune globulin when evacuation occurs at 12 weeks or later. Hysterectomy is optional only after childbearing and does not remove the need for monitoring. Routine prophylactic chemotherapy is not recommended. Medical evacuation is avoided because it increases hemorrhage and embolization of tissue. Pathology of the products of conception confirms the diagnosis, and hCG follow up continues afterward.

items.stem: A 59-year-old woman has a unifocal vulvar squamous cell carcinoma measuring 1.5 cm with 0.8 mm of stromal invasion. What is the appropriate surgical management?
options: Radical vulvectomy with bilateral inguinofemoral dissection
Sentinel node biopsy followed by chemoradiation
Wide local excision without lymph node evaluation
items.explanation: Stage IA vulvar cancer is a lesion 2 cm or smaller with invasion of 1 mm or less, and it is treated by wide local excision without nodal evaluation because nodal spread is negligible. Radical vulvectomy with dissection and exenteration are excessive and cause lymphedema and morbidity. Sentinel biopsy is for larger or deeper tumors.

items.stem: A 54-year-old woman's routine mammogram is read as a suspicious abnormality, category 4 of the Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System. What is the next step?
options: Return to routine screening in 12 months
Short-interval follow up imaging in 6 months
items.explanation: Category 4 means suspicious, and the action is biopsy, preferably core needle biopsy because it gives tissue architecture and receptor testing. Routine screening is for categories 1 and 2, and short-interval follow up is for category 3. Fine needle aspiration offers less information and is not preferred. Reconciling examination, imaging, and pathology prevents false reassurance when results disagree with each other.

items.stem: A 52-year-old woman taking tamoxifen for early breast cancer has no bleeding or other symptoms. She asks whether she needs routine endometrial testing. What is the best advice?
options: Annual endometrial biopsy for the duration of therapy
Stop tamoxifen and begin cyclic progestin
No routine testing, but report any bleeding promptly
items.explanation: Tamoxifen acts as an estrogen agonist in the uterus and raises endometrial cancer risk, but asymptomatic women are not screened with ultrasonography or biopsy. Counseling about prompt reporting of any bleeding is the key step, and bleeding triggers sampling. Stopping the drug and adding progestin are unjustified without a finding. Counseling about prompt reporting of bleeding therefore matters more than any scheduled test in a woman without symptoms.

items.stem: A 54-year-old woman has endometrial cancer with absent MLH1 protein on immunohistochemistry. Which test should be performed next to separate sporadic from hereditary disease?
items.explanation: When MLH1 protein is absent, tumor MLH1 promoter methylation is tested next, because methylation indicates a sporadic tumor rather than a germline cause. If methylation is absent, germline testing follows genetic counseling. BRCA testing addresses a different syndrome, and CA-125 and repeat biopsy do not clarify mismatch repair status. Germline testing follows genetic counseling only when methylation is absent, which saves needless testing.

items.stem: A 71-year-old woman has a single, firm, ulcerated vulvar lesion beside the clitoris. She has long-standing lichen sclerosus and a negative HPV test. Which statement about the likely precursor is most accurate?
options: Differentiated VIN is HPV unrelated and arises in lichen sclerosus
Usual-type VIN is the typical precursor in older women with lichen sclerosus
A precursor lesion is always multifocal and HPV positive
Differentiated VIN rarely progresses to invasive cancer
items.explanation: Differentiated VIN occurs in older women on a background of chronic inflammation such as lichen sclerosus, is unrelated to HPV, is usually a single lesion, and often carries a TP53 mutation. It progresses to invasion faster than the usual type. The HPV-driven usual type is multifocal and affects younger women. Any ulcerated lesion requires biopsy.

items.stem: A 22-year-old woman has a routine cytology result of low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion. She has no prior abnormal results. Which management is most appropriate?
items.explanation: Women 21 to 24 are managed conservatively because low-grade lesions so often regress and treatment risks later preterm birth. Repeat testing at 1 year is the approach. Excision or conization is treatment for high-grade disease and is excessive here. Returning to the routine interval would be too long for a result that raises the risk estimate above baseline.

items.stem: A 32-year-old woman received chest radiation at age 16 for Hodgkin lymphoma. Which breast cancer screening strategy is most appropriate?
options: Mammography every 2 years without magnetic resonance imaging
Annual mammography plus magnetic resonance imaging
items.explanation: Women who received chest radiation between ages 10 and 30 are at high risk and are offered supplemental magnetic resonance imaging along with mammography. Biennial mammography alone and clinical examination alone underscreen. The Gail model is not used for women with prior chest radiation. Ultrasonography every 5 years is not an accepted strategy. Dense tissue both raises risk and masks lesions, which is why mammography alone may be insufficient.

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman has a complete hydatidiform mole removed by suction curettage. She is stable and wishes to know how her disease will be followed. Which plan is most appropriate?
options: A single hCG level at 6 weeks after evacuation
Pelvic ultrasonography monthly without hCG testing
Weekly hCG until undetectable three times in a row
Repeat curettage at 2 weeks to confirm clearance
items.explanation: Quantitative hCG is the tumor marker for trophoblastic disease and is followed weekly until three consecutive undetectable values, then monthly for a set period. One late level misses early plateau or rise. Ultrasonography cannot replace the marker, and routine repeat curettage is not indicated. Persistent disease is diagnosed from the hCG curve and treated with chemotherapy.

items.stem: A 42-year-old woman has had a solid organ transplant and takes long-term immunosuppression. Which statement about her cervical screening is correct?
options: She follows the average-risk schedule and stops at 65
She needs more intensive screening, continued for life
She needs screening only until age 50
She needs no screening once vaccinated
items.explanation: Women with immunosuppression, such as transplant recipients or those with HIV infection, are screened more intensively and for life, because persistent HPV infection progresses more often. Stopping at 65 applies to average-risk women with adequate negative screening. Vaccination does not change the schedule. Each exception either shortens the interval or ends screening, and immunosuppression is the exception that lengthens it.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman has gestational trophoblastic neoplasia diagnosed as a placental site trophoblastic tumor, confined to the uterus. She has completed childbearing. What is the preferred treatment?
items.explanation: Placental site and epithelioid trophoblastic tumors respond poorly to chemotherapy and are treated with hysterectomy when disease is confined to the uterus. Methotrexate, effective for low-risk disease from invasive mole or choriocarcinoma, is less useful here. Radiation is not standard, and observation would allow progression. Hysterectomy also avoids prolonged chemotherapy exposure in a disease that responds poorly to drugs.

items.stem: A 62-year-old woman has a red, eczematous vulvar plaque that has not responded to topical steroids. Biopsy shows Paget cells with intraepithelial adenocarcinoma. What is the best management?
options: Wide local excision with evaluation for an associated malignancy
Simple vulvectomy with no further evaluation
items.explanation: Extramammary Paget disease of the vulva is an intraepithelial adenocarcinoma treated by wide local excision. Because it can accompany an underlying breast, colorectal, or urothelial cancer, evaluation includes mammography and colonoscopy. Steroids and antifungals treat eczema and candidiasis, and their failure prompted the biopsy. Vulvectomy without searching for an associated primary cancer is incomplete and may miss a coexisting cancer.

items.stem: A 64-year-old woman has a 3 cm lateral vulvar squamous cell carcinoma with 4 mm invasion. Which approach to nodal evaluation is preferred?
options: Routine full bilateral inguinofemoral dissection in all cases
items.explanation: Larger or deeper unifocal vulvar tumors, generally under 4 cm, are evaluated with sentinel lymph node biopsy, which has largely replaced routine full dissection because it reduces lymphedema. Nodal evaluation cannot be omitted at this depth. Para-aortic nodes are not the first echelon, since spread goes first to inguinofemoral nodes. Tumors near the midline or involving the clitoris need bilateral nodal evaluation instead.

items.stem: A 68-year-old woman has a 3 cm squamous cell carcinoma of the mid vagina. Cervix, vulva, and endometrium are normal on evaluation. Which primary treatment is most appropriate?
options: Observation with repeat biopsy in 6 months
items.explanation: Vaginal cancer is usually treated with radiation, often external beam combined with brachytherapy. Surgery is limited to small upper vaginal lesions. Primary vaginal cancer is diagnosed only after cervix, vulva, and endometrium are excluded. Methotrexate treats trophoblastic disease, and delay for observation would let an invasive cancer progress. Surveillance after treatment includes regular examination of the vagina because recurrence is often local.

items.stem: A 41-year-old woman at average risk asks when to begin mammography. Which recommendation reflects the Task Force screening schedule?
items.explanation: The Task Force recommends screening mammography every 2 years from age 40 through 74, while other organizations accept annual screening and shared decisions about start age. Starting at 35 or waiting until 50 or 55 does not match any mainstream average-risk schedule. Women at high risk are offered supplemental magnetic resonance imaging. Women at high risk by family history or prior chest radiation are offered supplemental imaging as well.

items.stem: A 63-year-old woman has grade 1 endometrioid adenocarcinoma on biopsy. What is the standard surgical approach?
options: Radical hysterectomy with neoadjuvant chemotherapy first
items.explanation: Staging of uterine cancer is surgical and consists of hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymph node assessment, with sentinel node mapping now common. Progestin after curettage is for selected fertility-seeking women after specialist review. A supracervical hysterectomy leaves the cervix and gives incomplete staging, and radical hysterectomy is excessive. Nodal status and myometrial invasion on the specimen then influence any adjuvant treatment decisions.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman has stage I gestational trophoblastic neoplasia with a FIGO prognostic score of 4 after molar evacuation. She wants future pregnancy. Which treatment is most appropriate?
options: Multiagent regimen with etoposide and cisplatin
items.explanation: A prognostic score of 6 or less defines low-risk disease, which is treated with single-agent methotrexate or dactinomycin and is cured in nearly all patients, preserving fertility. Multiagent therapy is reserved for scores of 7 or more. Hysterectomy is unnecessary in a woman who wants children. Radiation has no routine role in this disease. Response is judged by hCG remission, and relapse is monitored for 12 months after the marker normalizes.

items.stem: A 9-year-old girl has vulvar itching and thin white skin with fissures around the vulva and anus. Which statement about her condition is most accurate?
options: It can affect prepubertal girls and is treated with a potent topical steroid
It is a sexually transmitted infection requiring partner treatment
It resolves permanently after a short antifungal course
items.explanation: Lichen sclerosus is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis, most common after menopause but also seen in girls before puberty. Treatment is a potent topical corticosteroid such as clobetasol, with maintenance and long-term follow up. It is not infectious, so partner treatment and antifungals do not help, and it is controlled rather than cured. Long-term follow up is needed because a minority of affected patients eventually develop squamous carcinoma.

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman with breast cancer will begin cyclophosphamide chemotherapy within 2 weeks and wishes to have children later. Which fertility preservation step is most appropriate?
options: Reassurance that fertility will recover fully
Oocyte or embryo cryopreservation before treatment
items.explanation: Fertility is protected before gonadotoxic treatment by oocyte or embryo cryopreservation, and a gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist may be added during chemotherapy for some women. Alkylating agents such as cyclophosphamide carry the highest risk of ovarian failure, so reassurance is inaccurate. Tamoxifen does not protect the ovary, and radiation damages it. Referral to a reproductive specialist should occur before treatment so that stimulation does not delay cancer therapy.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 14 weeks of gestation has CIN 3 on colposcopic biopsy, with no suspicion of invasion. What is the appropriate management?
options: Loop excision of the transformation zone now
Cold knife conization now for definitive care
items.explanation: In pregnancy, CIN 2 or 3 is observed rather than treated unless invasion is suspected. Biopsy remains safe, but endocervical curettage is not performed, and conization is reserved for suspected invasive disease because it risks hemorrhage and pregnancy loss. Reassessment after delivery allows definitive management of the precancer. Reassessment after delivery then allows definitive treatment, and the plan is shared with the patient.

items.stem: A 32-year-old breast cancer survivor taking tamoxifen has bothersome hot flashes and requests treatment. Which medication is most appropriate?
items.explanation: Nonhormonal options such as venlafaxine or gabapentin are appropriate for vasomotor symptoms in survivors. Systemic estrogen is avoided after breast cancer. Paroxetine and fluoxetine inhibit CYP2D6, reducing activation of tamoxifen, so they are avoided in women taking it. Bone health and distress screening also belong in every survivorship visit for these women, whatever agent is chosen. Bone health and distress screening also belong in every survivorship visit for these women.

items.stem: A 67-year-old woman has had three consecutive normal cytology results, the latest 2 years ago. She has no history of CIN 2 or higher. Which recommendation is appropriate at this visit?
options: Continue cytology every 3 years for life
Switch to annual cytology after age 65
items.explanation: Screening may stop at 65 after adequate negative prior screening, generally three consecutive negative cytology results or two negative cotests within 10 years with the most recent within 5 years, and no CIN 2 or higher in the past 25 years. She meets these criteria. Continuing for life or intensifying is reserved for immunosuppressed women. Colposcopy is not needed without an abnormal result.

items.stem: A 58-year-old woman, para 2, reports one episode of light vaginal bleeding after 9 years without menses. She has no risk factors. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows an endometrial thickness of 3 mm. What is the best management?
options: Reassurance with return for any recurrent bleeding
items.explanation: An endometrial thickness of 4 mm or less carries a very low cancer risk, so observation is acceptable after a first episode. Recurrent or persistent bleeding would then call for tissue sampling. Hysteroscopy with curettage and hysterectomy are excessive for a thin stripe. Progestin therapy would be an empirical treatment that treats nothing demonstrated and could delay the diagnosis if bleeding returns.

items.stem: A 34-year-old woman has milky discharge from both nipples that appears only with compression. She has regular menses, the breast examination is normal, and her pregnancy test is negative. What is the best initial evaluation?
items.explanation: Bilateral, milky, expressed discharge in a nonpregnant woman suggests galactorrhea, so the first tests are prolactin and thyroid-stimulating hormone, after excluding pregnancy and reviewing medications. Ductography and duct excision serve spontaneous, unilateral, bloody or serous discharge that may signal a papilloma or cancer. Reassurance alone skips a treatable endocrine cause such as hypothyroidism or a prolactinoma.

items.stem: A 36-year-old woman, para 3, has adenocarcinoma in situ on loop excision with negative margins. She has completed childbearing. Which management is recommended?
items.explanation: Adenocarcinoma in situ can skip lesions in the canal, so even with clean margins, hysterectomy is recommended after childbearing is complete. Surveillance alone is reserved for women who want fertility. Repeated excisions do not solve skip lesions, and radiation has no role for an in situ lesion. Early excision with clean margins is therefore not enough to remove the risk in the remaining canal.

items.stem: A 48-year-old woman has a well-demarcated, red, weeping vulvar plaque that has not responded to topical steroid or antifungal treatment for 3 months. Biopsy shows large pale intraepidermal cells consistent with Paget disease. What additional evaluation is indicated?
options: Search for an underlying or distant adenocarcinoma
Sentinel node biopsy only, without other imaging
Repeat topical steroid therapy for another 3 months
items.explanation: Extramammary Paget disease is usually confined to the epithelium, but a minority of cases accompany an underlying vulvar gland adenocarcinoma or a cancer elsewhere. Evaluation therefore covers the breast, cervix, colon, and urinary tract. Further steroid therapy repeats the failed approach. Treatment is wide local excision, with long follow up because the disease extends past the visible edge.

items.stem: A 50-year-old woman has screening mammography reported as Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System category 3. What is the recommended action?
options: Short-interval imaging follow up in 6 months
items.explanation: Category 3 means probably benign, with a malignancy risk below 2 percent, and management is short-interval follow up imaging. Routine screening applies to categories 1 and 2. Biopsy is reserved for category 4 and 5, and surgical referral for category 5. Reassurance with a defined short follow up confirms stability and avoids unnecessary biopsy. Stable appearance on follow up imaging lets the woman avoid an unnecessary biopsy while risk stays low.

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman notices a painless, smooth, mobile 2 cm right breast mass. Examination shows no skin change or axillary adenopathy. Which study should be obtained first?
options: Magnetic resonance imaging of both breasts
items.explanation: In women under 30, ultrasonography is the first study for a palpable mass because dense breast tissue limits mammography and radiation exposure is best avoided. It separates solid from cystic lesions and guides sampling. Magnetic resonance imaging is not a first-line tool for a palpable mass. Excision before imaging and sampling skips the triple assessment of examination, imaging, and tissue.

items.stem: A 66-year-old woman has endometrial cancer on staging. Molecular classification shows a p53-abnormal tumor. Compared with other molecular groups, how is her prognosis best described?
options: The most favorable of the four groups
The poorest of the four molecular groups
Dependent only on tumor mismatch repair status
items.explanation: The molecular classification divides endometrial cancer into POLE-mutated, mismatch repair deficient, no specific molecular profile, and p53 abnormal. POLE-mutated tumors have an excellent prognosis, while p53-abnormal tumors have the poorest. Adjuvant therapy is guided by stage, grade, and molecular group together, so p53 status alone does not set the plan. Adjuvant therapy is guided by stage, grade, and molecular group together, so no single feature decides care.

items.stem: A 55-year-old woman has a 1.5 cm ulcerated vulvar lesion that has been treated with antifungal cream for 3 months without improvement. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Switch to a stronger topical corticosteroid
Continue antifungal therapy for 3 more months
items.explanation: A persistently ulcerated, raised, or pigmented vulvar lesion requires tissue diagnosis before any treatment. Empirical treatment for weeks without a biopsy is the error that delays recognition of vulvar carcinoma. A stronger steroid or more antifungal agent only extends the delay. Cryotherapy destroys the tissue needed for pathology. Pathology of the biopsy, not appearance, separates a benign dermatosis from a precancer or cancer.

items.stem: A 38-year-old woman at average genetic risk requests permanent contraception and is scheduled for a laparoscopic procedure. Given current understanding of ovarian cancer origin, which approach is preferred?
items.explanation: High-grade serous carcinoma frequently arises from the fimbrial end of the fallopian tube, so opportunistic salpingectomy in place of ligation lowers future risk without removing the ovaries or inducing menopause. Clip ligation leaves the fimbriae in place. Oophorectomy has no indication in an average-risk woman and causes premature menopause. Lower risk without surgical menopause makes this approach attractive for women at average genetic risk.

items.stem: A 38-year-old woman has a 4.5 cm cervical tumor confined to the cervix, staged IB3 by the 2018 FIGO system. Which treatment is most appropriate?
items.explanation: Locally advanced disease from stage IB3 through IVA is treated with chemoradiation including cisplatin. Early disease, such as stage IA and small IB1 tumors, is treated surgically. Conization is for precancer or microinvasion in selected women. Dactinomycin is a trophoblastic neoplasia drug with no role in cervical cancer. Early disease is treated surgically, and this boundary of tumor size is a frequent examination point.

items.stem: A 35-year-old premenopausal woman has an incidental 4 cm thin-walled, unilocular, anechoic ovarian cyst without septations or flow. She has no symptoms. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Serum CA-125 and immediate staging surgery
items.explanation: A simple, thin-walled unilocular cyst is almost always benign, and in a premenopausal woman it is typically observed with follow-up ultrasonography. Oophorectomy is excessive. Aspiration is avoided in possible malignancy because spill upstages cancer, and CA-125 is raised in many benign states, so it adds little here. Findings are interpreted together with menopausal status, and ultrasound characterization always comes first.

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman delivered at term 3 months ago and now has persistent bleeding and cough. Chest radiography shows multiple nodules. Which test is most appropriate first?
items.explanation: Choriocarcinoma can follow a term birth, a miscarriage, or an ectopic pregnancy, so unexplained bleeding or metastases in a woman of reproductive age warrants an hCG. The lung is the most frequent metastatic site, and biopsy is avoided because of hemorrhage risk. Culture and imaging alone do not identify the diagnosis. Imaging of the pelvis and further imaging follow once the hCG confirms trophoblastic disease.

items.stem: A 62-year-old postmenopausal woman has osteoporosis and elevated breast cancer risk by a validated model. She has an intact uterus and no thromboembolism history. Which chemopreventive agent has the advantage of not raising endometrial cancer risk?
items.explanation: Raloxifene is limited to postmenopausal women and, unlike tamoxifen, does not raise endometrial cancer risk, while also helping bone density. Tamoxifen increases endometrial cancer and thromboembolism. Unopposed estrogen raises endometrial cancer risk markedly in a woman with a uterus. Aromatase inhibitors cause bone loss, a drawback in osteoporosis. Benefit must be weighed against harm for each woman, and duration is generally about five years.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome has four menses per year and body mass index of 35. Which counseling best addresses her endometrial cancer risk?
options: No intervention is needed until age 50
Regulate cycles with progestin and encourage weight loss
Unopposed estrogen cycles to induce regular withdrawal bleeding
items.explanation: Chronic anovulation exposes the endometrium to unopposed estrogen, and obesity adds peripheral estrone production. Cycle regulation with progestin or combined pills lowers risk, as does weight loss. Waiting until 50 allows years of exposure, routine annual biopsy is not indicated without symptoms, and giving estrogen alone worsens the process. Counseling about weight loss and cycle regulation is a central part of prevention in this condition.

items.stem: A 55-year-old woman with no family history of cancer asks about annual CA-125 and transvaginal ultrasonography to screen for ovarian cancer. What should she be told?
options: These tests are not recommended for average-risk screening
The combination reduces ovarian cancer mortality
Ultrasonography is recommended but CA-125 is not
Both are recommended every 6 months after age 50
items.explanation: No screening test has reduced ovarian cancer mortality in average-risk women, and ultrasonography with CA-125 is not recommended. CA-125 is raised in many benign states, leading to false positives and unnecessary surgery. Women with vague symptoms or a strong family history should be evaluated or referred for genetic counseling instead. Women with persistent symptoms or strong family history should be evaluated and offered genetic counseling instead.

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman has progressive hirsutism and voice deepening. Pelvic ultrasonography shows a solid unilateral ovarian mass, and testosterone is markedly elevated. Which tumor is most likely?
options: Granulosa cell tumor of the ovary
items.explanation: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors secrete androgens and cause virilization, and they are associated with DICER1 variants. Granulosa cell tumors secrete estrogen and inhibin. Dysgerminoma raises lactate dehydrogenase, and yolk sac tumor raises alpha-fetoprotein. Neither produces the androgen excess described here. These tumors are rare, usually occur in young women, and are often managed with fertility-sparing surgery after staging.

items.stem: A 58-year-old woman has well-controlled vulvar lichen sclerosus on maintenance steroid. She asks why follow up must continue. Which explanation is most accurate?
options: A minority of patients eventually develop squamous cell carcinoma
The disease is cured after one year of treatment
It converts to Paget disease in most women
Follow up is needed only if she becomes pregnant
items.explanation: Lichen sclerosus is controlled rather than cured, and a minority of women develop vulvar squamous cell carcinoma, so lifelong follow up and biopsy of suspicious or unresponsive lesions are needed. It does not convert to Paget disease, and the schedule does not depend on pregnancy, which is uncommon at this age. Biopsy is also indicated for atypical features or lesions that fail to respond to treatment.

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman has gestational trophoblastic neoplasia with lung metastases and a FIGO prognostic score of 9. Which treatment is most appropriate?
options: Biopsy of the lung lesions followed by observation
items.explanation: A score of 7 or more is high risk and is treated with multiagent chemotherapy. Single-agent methotrexate is for low-risk disease. Hysterectomy alone does not treat metastases. Biopsy of metastases is avoided because of hemorrhage risk, and observation would allow progression of a highly chemosensitive cancer. Cure is expected in most patients, and monitoring continues for 12 months after remission.

items.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 22 weeks of gestation has lymphoma needing systemic chemotherapy. She asks about timing near delivery. What is the most appropriate counseling?
options: Continue chemotherapy through the day of delivery
Stop chemotherapy about 3 weeks before expected delivery
Delay all chemotherapy until after birth at 40 weeks
Begin chemotherapy only in the first trimester
items.explanation: Many regimens may be given in the second and third trimesters, and treatment is stopped about 3 weeks before expected delivery to avoid neutropenia and bleeding at birth. Chemotherapy is avoided in the first trimester because of organogenesis. Delaying treatment when maternal survival depends on it is not appropriate. Chemotherapy is avoided in the first trimester because organogenesis makes malformations more likely during that period.

items.stem: A 47-year-old woman has an increased breast cancer risk by a validated model and no personal history of thromboembolism. Which statement about chemoprevention counseling is correct?
options: Raloxifene increases the risk of endometrial cancer in postmenopausal women
Aromatase inhibitors are preferred before menopause
Tamoxifen raises venous thromboembolism and endometrial cancer risk
Chemoprevention lowers risk of receptor-negative cancers
items.explanation: Tamoxifen works before and after menopause but increases venous thromboembolism, endometrial cancer, and cataracts. Raloxifene is for postmenopausal women and does not raise endometrial cancer risk. Aromatase inhibitors are used only after menopause. Risk reduction applies chiefly to estrogen receptor positive cancers, so benefits and harms are weighed for each woman. Risk reduction mainly applies to estrogen receptor positive cancers, so shared decision making precedes any drug.

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman has a routine cotest showing atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance with a positive high-risk HPV result. She has no prior abnormal results. What is the next step?
items.explanation: An HPV-positive result with atypical squamous cells carries an immediate CIN 3 risk above the colposcopy threshold of about 4 percent, so colposcopy is indicated. Repeating testing delays evaluation of a risk that already warrants a look. Excision without biopsy is reserved for the highest risk tier. An HPV-negative result would instead allow a return to routine screening.

items.stem: A 58-year-old woman has biopsy-proven vulvar lichen sclerosus, well controlled on topical clobetasol. What long-term counseling is most appropriate?
options: The condition resolves after menopause and needs no follow-up
Risk of melanoma is increased in the affected skin
Sexual partners should be treated to prevent recurrence
A small risk of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma requires regular follow-up
items.explanation: Vulvar lichen sclerosus is a chronic condition that carries a small lifetime risk of squamous cell carcinoma, so treatment and periodic examination are needed, with biopsy of any ulcer or thickened lesion. It does not resolve spontaneously with menopause. Melanoma risk is not increased. The disease is not infectious, so treating partners has no effect.

items.stem: A 61-year-old woman has recurrent postmenopausal bleeding. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows a 7 mm endometrial stripe, and office biopsy yields insufficient tissue. What is the next step?
options: Hysteroscopy with directed biopsy and curettage
Observation, since insufficient tissue means benign
items.explanation: A thick stripe or persistent bleeding calls for tissue, and when an office biopsy is nondiagnostic, hysteroscopy with directed biopsy and curettage is added, particularly for focal lesions such as polyps. Insufficient tissue does not equal benign pathology. Cytology is not a screening test for endometrial cancer, and repeated imaging alone never provides reassurance when bleeding persists.

items.stem: A 26-year-old woman has a 9 cm solid pelvic mass. Serum lactate dehydrogenase is markedly elevated, while alpha-fetoprotein and hCG are normal. Which tumor is most likely?
items.explanation: Dysgerminoma is the most common malignant ovarian germ cell tumor and is characterized by raised lactate dehydrogenase. A yolk sac tumor raises alpha-fetoprotein, and embryonal carcinoma raises alpha-fetoprotein and hCG together. Mature cystic teratoma is benign and has no characteristic marker elevation. Dysgerminoma is highly sensitive to chemotherapy and radiation, so fertility-sparing surgery is common.

items.stem: A 62-year-old woman has abdominal bloating and early satiety. Imaging shows bilateral complex adnexal masses with ascites, and CA-125 is markedly elevated. Which step is most appropriate?
options: Ultrasound-guided aspiration of the largest cyst
items.explanation: A mass with suspicious features, bilateral involvement, and ascites calls for surgery by a gynecologic oncologist, who can stage and cytoreduce. Cyst aspiration or biopsy is avoided because spill upstages a malignancy. Repeating the marker delays care. Contraceptive pills lower future risk in healthy women but do not treat a suspected cancer. Surgery by an oncologist also allows complete staging and cytoreduction at the same operation.

items.stem: A 60-year-old woman with stage III ovarian cancer and a BRCA2 variant responded to carboplatin and paclitaxel. She begins olaparib maintenance. Which rare serious complication should she be counseled about?
items.explanation: Poly-ADP-ribose polymerase inhibitors cause anemia and fatigue commonly, and rarely myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia. Benefit is greatest in BRCA-mutated or homologous recombination deficient tumors. Hemorrhagic cystitis follows cyclophosphamide or ifosfamide, cardiomyopathy follows anthracyclines, and persistent neuropathy follows platinum and taxane drugs, not these inhibitors. Complete blood counts are monitored during therapy, and unexplained persistent cytopenias should prompt evaluation.

items.stem: A 29-year-old woman received the full HPV vaccine series at age 14. She asks whether she still needs cervical screening. What is the correct advice?
options: No, vaccination eliminates the need for screening
Yes, screening follows the usual schedule for her age
Yes, but with annual cytology for life
Only if she develops symptoms of cervical disease
items.explanation: HPV vaccination does not change the screening schedule, because the vaccine does not cover every oncogenic type and does not treat existing infection. At 29 she follows the average-risk schedule of cytology every 3 years. Vaccinated women are not screened annually, and screening is never symptom triggered because precancer is asymptomatic. The vaccine protects against the most common oncogenic types but never replaces screening afterward.

items.stem: A 41-year-old woman, para 3, who has completed childbearing, carries a germline MSH2 pathogenic variant. She has no cancer. Which counseling is most appropriate regarding her gynecologic risk?
options: Annual transvaginal ultrasonography alone for endometrial surveillance
Cervical cytology alone is sufficient for endometrial risk
Offer risk-reducing hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
Surgery is contraindicated until cancer is diagnosed
items.explanation: Lynch syndrome carries a high lifetime risk of endometrial and ovarian cancer, and ultrasonography does not reliably detect early disease. After childbearing, risk-reducing hysterectomy with salpingo-oophorectomy is the preferred strategy, and endometrial biopsy surveillance is an option until then. Cervical cytology samples the wrong organ. Waiting for cancer defeats prevention. Genetic counseling and testing also help identify relatives who can pursue prevention.

items.stem: A 25-year-old woman has a persistently detectable hCG 2 weeks after evacuation of a complete mole and requests contraception. Which method is most appropriate now?
options: A copper intrauterine device placed today
A levonorgestrel intrauterine device placed today
No contraception, since pregnancy is unlikely
items.explanation: Effective contraception is required during surveillance, because a rising hCG from a new pregnancy cannot be distinguished from persistent disease. Hormonal pills and progestin methods are acceptable. An intrauterine device is placed only after hCG is undetectable, because of the perforation risk in a soft uterus. Assuming no pregnancy risk undermines monitoring. Compliance with follow up is the key determinant of safety during this surveillance period.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman with prior gastric cancer has bilateral ovarian masses. Frozen section shows mucin-filled signet ring cells. Which diagnosis is most likely?
items.explanation: A Krukenberg tumor is a metastatic mucinous tumor from the gastrointestinal tract, typically bilateral with signet ring cells. Mature cystic teratoma is benign with mature tissue elements. Sertoli-Leydig tumors secrete androgens and are unilateral, and borderline serous tumors lack stromal invasion and signet ring morphology. Markers aid diagnosis and monitoring but pathology remains the final arbiter for any ovarian tumor.

items.stem: A 66-year-old woman has locally advanced vulvar squamous cell carcinoma involving the urethra and anus. Which approach is most appropriate to avoid exenteration?
items.explanation: Advanced vulvar tumors may be treated with chemoradiation to avoid pelvic exenteration, with surgery for residual disease. Wide local excision alone cannot clear a tumor involving the urethra and anus. Observation lets invasive cancer progress. Imiquimod treats selected high-grade intraepithelial lesions, not invasive carcinoma. Complete response reduces the need for pelvic exenteration and its major effect on urinary and bowel function.

items.stem: A 22-year-old woman has a smooth, mobile breast mass. Core biopsy shows fibroadenoma, concordant with ultrasonographic findings. She has no symptoms and no rapid growth. What is the best management?
items.explanation: When core biopsy confirms fibroadenoma and imaging agrees, observation is reasonable. Excision is reserved for growth, symptoms, or patient preference. Wide excision is the approach if a phyllodes tumor is suspected from rapid growth. Mastectomy and tamoxifen have no role in a benign concordant lesion. Growth, new symptoms, or concern about phyllodes tumor would change this plan and favor excision.

items.stem: Which mechanism best explains why tamoxifen increases the risk of endometrial cancer?
options: Direct mutation of mismatch repair genes
Partial estrogen agonist effect on the endometrium
Conversion of androstenedione to estrone in fat
items.explanation: Tamoxifen blocks estrogen in breast tissue but acts as an estrogen agonist in the uterus, causing proliferation and raising endometrial cancer risk. It does not mutate mismatch repair genes, which is the Lynch pathway. Peripheral aromatization of androstenedione in adipose tissue explains the obesity risk, and suppressing progesterone is not its mechanism. Cell proliferation then follows persistent stimulation, and the effect explains why bleeding in these patients needs sampling.

items.stem: A 29-year-old woman has bilateral milky nipple discharge elicited only by compression. She takes an antipsychotic medication, and breast examination is otherwise normal. Which initial evaluation is most appropriate?
options: Cytologic examination of the discharge fluid
items.explanation: Bilateral, multiductal, compression-elicited milky discharge is physiologic and prompts a pregnancy test, prolactin, and thyroid testing with medication review, since antipsychotics raise prolactin. Excision is reserved for spontaneous, unilateral, single-duct discharge. Fluid cytology has little value, and biopsy of the pituitary is never an initial test. Spontaneous unilateral discharge from a single duct would instead point toward an intraductal papilloma.

items.stem: A 23-year-old woman, gravida 0, presents for her first well-woman visit and asks which cervical screening test she should have and how often. What is the recommended approach?
options: Cotesting with cytology and HPV every 5 years
Cytology alone every year until age 30
High-risk HPV testing alone every 3 years
items.explanation: For women 21 to 29, the Task Force recommends cytology alone every 3 years. HPV testing is not used in this age group because infections are common and usually transient, so testing would lead to unnecessary colposcopy. Cotesting and HPV-alone strategies enter at age 30. Annual cytology adds harm without added benefit in average-risk women. Screening does not begin before 21 regardless of sexual history.

items.stem: A 34-year-old woman at 22 weeks of gestation has a suspicious abdominal mass and the team needs additional staging imaging. Which modality is preferred?
options: Nuclear medicine bone scan as the first study
items.explanation: Ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging without gadolinium are preferred in pregnancy. Gadolinium is avoided. When a radiograph or CT is necessary, the fetal dose is far below the threshold for harm, so a needed study is not withheld. Termination is not required in most cases, and a nuclear scan is not a first choice. Delivery planning, timing of any chemotherapy, and fetal monitoring are coordinated with maternal-fetal medicine.

items.stem: A 63-year-old woman has postmenopausal bleeding and a unilateral adnexal mass. Endometrial biopsy shows hyperplasia. Which tumor marker is most likely elevated?
items.explanation: A granulosa cell tumor secretes estrogen and inhibin, causing postmenopausal bleeding, endometrial hyperplasia, and in children precocious puberty. Alpha-fetoprotein marks yolk sac tumor, lactate dehydrogenase marks dysgerminoma, and hCG marks embryonal carcinoma or choriocarcinoma. These markers aid diagnosis and monitoring but never replace pathology. Estrogen effects also explain the association with endometrial hyperplasia and sometimes cancer in these women.

items.stem: A 36-year-old woman has bilateral cyclic breast pain before menses. Examination and age-appropriate imaging are normal. Which management is most appropriate?
items.explanation: Mastalgia is rarely a sign of cancer. With normal findings, treatment is reassurance, a well-fitted supportive bra, and topical or oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, plus review of contributing medications. Excisional biopsy of a presumed benign process is not required. Tamoxifen and mastectomy are far out of proportion to a benign symptom. Pain that is focal and persistent deserves targeted imaging, even when the rest of the evaluation is reassuring.

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman has a stage I serous borderline ovarian tumor found at surgery, with no invasive implants. She desires future fertility. What is the appropriate management?
options: Adjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel for six cycles
Surgery alone with preservation of the uterus and remaining ovary
items.explanation: Borderline tumors, also called tumors of low malignant potential, are treated with surgery alone and have an excellent outlook. Fertility-sparing surgery is reasonable after complete staging. Chemotherapy is given only if invasive implants are found, and maintenance inhibitors are for invasive disease with a BRCA variant or homologous recombination deficiency. Pathologic staging still requires washings and peritoneal biopsies to confirm that the disease is truly early.

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman has a cervical biopsy showing CIN 3 after an abnormal screening test, and colposcopy is satisfactory. Which management is most appropriate?
items.explanation: CIN 3 is a true precancer with a substantial risk of progression to invasive cancer, so excisional or ablative treatment is indicated, and loop electrosurgical excision is standard when colposcopy is satisfactory. Surveillance alone is appropriate for CIN 1 and for selected young women with CIN 2. Hysterectomy is excessive for a precancer that can be removed locally while preserving fertility.

items.stem: A 36-year-old woman, para 3, has completed childbearing. Genetic testing shows a pathogenic BRCA1 variant. She has no cancer. When is risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy generally recommended for her?
options: At age 45 to 50, once menopause is near
Only after an abnormal CA-125 level
Between age 35 and 40, after childbearing is complete
At age 60, with annual ultrasonography until then
items.explanation: For BRCA1 carriers, risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy is advised at 35 to 40 years after childbearing, because ovarian cancer risk rises earlier than in BRCA2 carriers. Waiting until 45 or later leaves years of preventable risk. CA-125 and ultrasonography do not detect early ovarian cancer reliably, so surveillance is no substitute. Premenopausal surgery also lowers breast cancer risk.

items.stem: A 46-year-old woman has a firm 3 cm Bartholin gland mass that was drained twice and recurred. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Excision or biopsy of the mass
Repeat incision and drainage with a Word catheter
items.explanation: A new or recurrent Bartholin gland mass in a woman over 40 is biopsied or excised, because drainage will not treat a Bartholin carcinoma. Catheter drainage and marsupialization are appropriate for benign abscess or cyst in younger women but give no tissue. Antibiotics do not address a solid or persistent lesion. Tissue diagnosis matters more than appearance, and persistent or solid lesions need pathology before any treatment.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman who has completed childbearing underwent hysterectomy for a complete mole. She asks whether she still needs hCG monitoring. What is the correct answer?
options: No, hysterectomy removes all trophoblastic risk
Yes, because metastatic disease can still develop
Only if she becomes pregnant again
No, a single normal level suffices
items.explanation: Hysterectomy is an option after childbearing, but it does not remove the need for monitoring, because metastatic trophoblastic disease can still develop. Serial hCG remains the tumor marker. Pregnancy is not the trigger for testing, and a single normal value does not exclude a plateau or rise on later samples. Compliance with follow up is the key determinant of safety, and women who cannot return need careful counseling.

items.stem: A 58-year-old woman had optimal cytoreduction for stage IIIC high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma. Which standard first-line adjuvant chemotherapy should she receive?
items.explanation: Standard first-line chemotherapy for epithelial ovarian cancer is carboplatin with paclitaxel, given after surgery or as neoadjuvant therapy when upfront resection is unsafe. Bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin treat malignant germ cell tumors. Methotrexate treats low-risk trophoblastic disease, and tamoxifen has no first-line role. Bevacizumab may be added in selected patients, and maintenance therapy follows after response to platinum.

items.stem: A 30-year-old nonpregnant woman has CIN 2 on colposcopic biopsy. The transformation zone is fully visible, and she has completed childbearing. Which treatment is preferred?
items.explanation: CIN 2 or 3 is usually treated by excision, because it provides a specimen for margin assessment. Observation of CIN 2 is acceptable only in young women wishing fertility who can be followed reliably. Hysterectomy is excessive for CIN. Cisplatin is used with radiation for locally advanced invasive cervical cancer, not for precancer. Margin status on the excised specimen then guides follow up cytology and HPV testing after treatment.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman was exposed to diethylstilbestrol in utero. She asks about her cancer risk. Which malignancy is specifically increased?
options: Squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva
items.explanation: In utero diethylstilbestrol exposure causes clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina and cervix, vaginal adenosis, a T-shaped uterus, and higher risks of preterm birth and ectopic pregnancy. Exposed women need annual cytology with palpation and inspection of the vagina. Vulvar squamous carcinoma, ovarian serous carcinoma, and uterine sarcoma are not characteristic of this exposure, which is why the vagina itself is inspected.

items.stem: A 31-year-old nulligravid woman has endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia on biopsy and strongly desires future pregnancy. Imaging shows no myometrial invasion. Which plan is most appropriate?
options: Immediate hysterectomy without discussion of alternatives
Low-dose oral contraceptive with biopsy in 2 years
High-dose progestin with repeat biopsy every 3 to 6 months
items.explanation: Atypical hyperplasia is a true precursor, and hysterectomy is standard once childbearing is complete. A woman who wishes fertility may choose high-dose progestin with strict biopsy surveillance every 3 to 6 months, understanding the recurrence risk. Low-dose contraceptive pills and annual ultrasonography are insufficient. Hysterectomy follows if disease persists or after childbearing. Whichever route is chosen, the family must understand the recurrence risk and the need for close follow up.

items.stem: A 39-year-old obese woman has cytology showing atypical glandular cells. HPV testing is pending. Which evaluation is most appropriate?
options: Colposcopy with endocervical and endometrial sampling
Loop excision of the transformation zone only
items.explanation: Atypical glandular cells require colposcopy with endocervical sampling, and endometrial sampling is added from age 35, or earlier with risk factors such as obesity or abnormal bleeding. The glandular lesion may arise in the canal or uterus. Repeat cytology delays evaluation, and excision alone omits the endometrium. Infection does not explain glandular atypia. Management here follows risk, which is why age and risk factors change the extent of sampling.

items.stem: A 56-year-old postmenopausal woman has a rapidly enlarging presumed fibroid and a heterogeneous uterine mass with necrosis on imaging. Which statement best guides surgical planning?
options: Preoperative endometrial biopsy reliably excludes sarcoma
Morcellation is preferred to limit the incision
Avoid power morcellation because of possible sarcoma
items.explanation: Leiomyosarcoma has no reliable preoperative test and is usually found after surgery for a presumed fibroid. Rapid growth in a postmenopausal woman and necrosis raise suspicion. Power morcellation can disseminate an unsuspected sarcoma, so it is avoided, and contained techniques are used if morcellation is chosen. Imaging and markers cannot confirm the diagnosis. Counseling before surgery for presumed fibroids should therefore mention this uncommon but serious risk.

items.stem: A 36-week pregnant woman has stage IB cervical cancer diagnosed earlier in pregnancy. Which delivery plan is most appropriate?
items.explanation: Route of delivery follows the obstetric indication, except that a cervical cancer is delivered by cesarean birth. Passing through a tumor-bearing cervix risks hemorrhage and implantation of tumor at the episiotomy. Instrumented delivery is similarly inappropriate. Delivery is planned near term when possible, not at 28 weeks. Regional anesthesia and the timing of delivery are otherwise decided by obstetric indications.

items.stem: A 51-year-old woman has newly diagnosed high-grade serous ovarian cancer and no family history of cancer. Which statement about genetic testing is correct?
options: Testing is limited to women with an affected first-degree relative
Testing is indicated only if CA-125 exceeds 500
Testing is deferred until after menopause
Testing for every woman with epithelial ovarian cancer
items.explanation: Genetic testing is offered to every woman with epithelial ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal cancer regardless of family history, because results guide maintenance therapy with inhibitors and identify relatives who can pursue prevention. Restricting it to a family history, a marker level, or menopausal status would miss many carriers. Results obtained at diagnosis also shape maintenance and recurrence strategies, so testing should not be delayed.
